A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same bias-inheritance study. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and added analyses.

before.justification: V1 reports original experiments on biased synthetic-data augmentation and mitigation, including classification, hiring, salary recommendation, story generation, and iterative fine-tuning.

after.justification: V3 retains these empirical results and adds experiments with Qwen and DeepSeek models, together with statistical significance results.

M1.justification: The six-type generation framework and token-, mask-, and loss-based mitigation procedures remain unchanged, including the alignment objective and implementation descriptions. Renaming the 'Unbiased' prompt type to 'Neutral' does not change its prompt or procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same gender and cultural domains, ten tasks, training datasets, and seventeen evaluation datasets. Table 1 replaces a duplicated ToLD-Br-Homophobia entry with ToLD-Br-Misogyny, which v1 already describes as evaluated in Appendix B.1. The additional models use existing gender tasks.

E2.justification: The unaugmented and augmented controls and token-, mask-, and loss-based mitigation comparisons are retained, including the token/mask comparison for GPT-4o-mini. Qwen and DeepSeek are additional validation models; no competing mitigation method is added.

E3.justification: New Appendix E substantially expands model configurations: Qwen3-0.6B, 1.7B, 4B, and 8B, plus DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B, are evaluated on salary and hiring with 50% synthetic augmentation. The previously reported sample sizes, learning rates, epochs, metrics, and GPT-4o-mini scaling setting remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix E adds a systematic robustness and size-sensitivity analysis asking whether bias inheritance persists across model families and whether increasing model size mitigates it. This substantially extends the earlier Llama/GPT-4o-mini evidence. Existing multi-round, embedding-distribution, and mitigation analyses are retained.

E5.justification: New Appendix D and Table 7 introduce t-tests and p-values covering group comparisons, multi-round experiments, scaling, embeddings, and mitigation. V1 reports no corresponding significance tests. This addition does not establish additional independent training runs; the tests' sampling units and replicate counts remain unspecified.

E6.justification: Figure 13 adds salary and hiring results for five models, including differing directional shifts for Qwen and DeepSeek; Table 7 adds numerical significance results. Figures 4 and 10 change the gender attribution of hiring results. Figure 4 retains its bar values while swapping male/female labels, and Section 4.2 changes the emphasized larger male increase from 20%/50% to 5%/10% augmentation.

T1.justification: The dataset-union formulation, bias-ratio definition, and squared mean-embedding alignment loss are retained. Neither version supplies additional theorems or proofs, and the new empirical significance tests do not revise the mathematical framework.

C1.justification: The central bias-inheritance framework and three mitigation contributions remain. V3 qualifies the introduction's assertion that bias 'always' causes inheritance to 'can' cause inheritance and expands its stated empirical validation to multiple model families.

C2.justification: V3 newly acknowledges limitations from binary gender categories and US-centric salary evaluation. Appendix E adds the interpretation that increasing model size alone does not prevent inheritance and extends the discussion of model-dependent bias directions. The original three misalignment explanations and mitigation limitations remain.

D1.justification: V3 adds a code-availability statement and repository link in the first-page footnote. Core training hyperparameters, prompts, name lists, and mitigation implementation details are retained; the LoRA disclosure moves from Section 4.1 to Appendix B.5.

R1.justification: V3 adds explicit positioning relative to model-collapse research by Shumailov and Gerstgrasser and bias-transfer research by Steed, alongside Qwen and DeepSeek references. Several illustrative demographic-bias citations are removed. The central positioning around synthetic-data bias inheritance remains.

P1.justification: The main text is extensively condensed and edited, including reorganized introductory findings and streamlined related-work and mitigation subsections. Conclusion, limitations, and ethical considerations become separate sections, and the appendices are reorganized. Terminology changes from 'Unbiased' to 'Neutral' throughout.

P2.justification: The document changes from single-column to two-column layout, substantially resizing and relocating figures and tables. V3 adds Figure 13 and Table 7, revises hiring-plot labels and formatting, and renumbers retained appendix figures.

improvement.justification: The additional model and size checks broaden empirical support, while revised hiring labels and discussion improve internal consistency. Code access information and explicit applicability limitations also help. The gain is limited because the added model tests cover only salary and hiring, and Table 7 does not explain the sampling units or independent-run counts underlying its t-tests.
